_comment: GENERATED by pipeline/analysis/headline_figures.py. Do not edit by hand. Every value carries the SQL that derived it. A number rendered in prose must come from here.

registered_departures_2004_2025.note: People Slovak authorities recorded leaving, 2004-2025. SUSR om7011rr IN010079 at national level. A floor, not a count: deregistration is unenforced, so this counts only those who filed. Not comparable to the mirror figures, which stop at 2024.
registered_departures_2004_2025.sql: SELECT sum(value) AS value FROM s1 WHERE metric = 'migr_out' AND geo_level = 'nation' AND year BETWEEN 2004 AND 2025 AND age_bracket = 'all' AND sex = 'all' AND education = 'all'

cohort_retention_median.note: Median district cohort retention: 35-39 year olds in 2024 over 15-19 year olds in 2004, same district. Derived from SUSR om7007rr.
cohort_retention_median.sql: SELECT median(value) AS value FROM s1 WHERE metric = 'cohort_retention' AND geo_level = 'okres'

slovaks_in_cz_residents_2025.note: Slovak citizens RESIDENT in Czechia, CSU CIZ003T003, 2025. Distinct from the labour figure below, which is larger because it counts employment relationships including cross-border commuters.
slovaks_in_cz_residents_2025.sql: SELECT value FROM s2 WHERE metric = 'stock' AND source = 'csu_CIZ003T003' AND cz_geo_code = 'CZ' AND sex = 'all' AND pathway = 'all' AND year = 2025

slovaks_in_cz_labour_2024.note: Slovaks in the Czech LABOUR MARKET, CSU CIZ03, 2024: employees plus trade-licence holders. Not a count of residents.
slovaks_in_cz_labour_2024.sql: SELECT sum(value) AS value FROM s2 WHERE metric = 'stock' AND pathway = 'labour' AND year = 2024 AND sex = 'all' AND employment_status IN ('employed', 'self_employed')

diaspora_destinations_2020.note: Destinations with a non-zero Slovak-born stock in the 2020 UN DESA revision. The site previously said 87, which was the count of keys before an M49/ISO3 mapping bug was fixed.
diaspora_destinations_2020.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT destination_iso3) AS value FROM s3 WHERE metric = 'stock' AND slovak_def = 'born' AND year = 2020 AND value > 0

mirror_implied_departures_2004_2024.note: Departures implied by the registers of the 11 destination countries that counted Slovak citizens at both 1 Jan 2004 and 1 Jan 2025: rise in reported stock plus naturalisations over 2004-2024. A floor; the panel omits the UK, IE, ES, CH and FR. See 06-sources-page.md section 4a.

mirror_panel_countries.note: Destination countries in the 2004-2025 mirror panel.

mirror_registered_departures_2004_2024.note: SUSR registered departures over 2004-2024, the window the mirror comparison can speak to. The hero's 2004-2025 total is larger by the 2025 figure alone; the two reconcile exactly.

def_panel_countries.note: Destinations reporting BOTH a Slovak-born and a Slovak-citizen stock for 2020.
def_panel_countries.sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT destination_iso3, value FROM s3 WHERE slovak_def='born' AND metric='stock' AND year=2020 AND sex='all' AND source='un_desa_bilateral_2020'), c AS ( SELECT destination_iso3, value FROM s3 WHERE slovak_def='citizen' AND metric='stock' AND year=2020) SELECT count(*) n, sum(b.value) born, sum(c.value) citizen FROM b JOIN c USING(destination_iso3)

def_panel_born.note: Slovak-born on the matched panel. UN DESA's full total is 419,651 across 51 destinations, so the panel covers 72.8% of it.
def_panel_born.sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT destination_iso3, value FROM s3 WHERE slovak_def='born' AND metric='stock' AND year=2020 AND sex='all' AND source='un_desa_bilateral_2020'), c AS ( SELECT destination_iso3, value FROM s3 WHERE slovak_def='citizen' AND metric='stock' AND year=2020) SELECT count(*) n, sum(b.value) born, sum(c.value) citizen FROM b JOIN c USING(destination_iso3)

def_panel_citizen.note: Slovak citizens on the matched panel. Eurostat's full total is 297,234 across 25 destinations, so the panel covers 100.0% of it.
def_panel_citizen.sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT destination_iso3, value FROM s3 WHERE slovak_def='born' AND metric='stock' AND year=2020 AND sex='all' AND source='un_desa_bilateral_2020'), c AS ( SELECT destination_iso3, value FROM s3 WHERE slovak_def='citizen' AND metric='stock' AND year=2020) SELECT count(*) n, sum(b.value) born, sum(c.value) citizen FROM b JOIN c USING(destination_iso3)

diaspora_destinations_un_desa_2020.note: UN DESA 2020 destinations with a Slovak-born stock. This is the figure to quote for the diaspora's geographic spread; the any-source count is 52, differing by the United States alone, which UN DESA omits entirely.
diaspora_destinations_un_desa_2020.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT destination_iso3) FROM s3 WHERE slovak_def='born' AND metric='stock' AND year=2020 AND sex='all' AND source='un_desa_bilateral_2020'

susr_cubes_used.note: SUSR DataCube cubes feeding a rendered metric. 13 directories exist, 12 hold data (om7009rr returned none), and these are the ones the output parquets attribute.
susr_cubes_used.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT source) FROM s1 WHERE source LIKE 'susr_%'

csu_tables_used.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT source) FROM s2 WHERE source LIKE 'csu_%'

oecd_datasets_used.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT source) FROM s3 WHERE source LIKE 'oecd_%'
